questions.stem: How is innate immunity different from adaptive immunity?

options.text: Innate immunity does not require signaling/expression of any new genes to be fully functional.
Innate immunity may function readily without a previous exposure to microbes.
Innate immunity has cellular receptors, but they bind non-specific ligands.
Innate immunity functions without the need for cellular receptors.

questions.answerRationale: Starred in your Ch 9 chapter file.

questions.stem: Which of these is beyond adaptation for the adaptive immune system?

options.text: Receptor ligand binding, signaling events, and expression of new genes.
Expression of different sets of genes in response to infection by different pathogens.
Mutating genes and selecting more effective mutant cells to combat future infections.

questions.answerRationale: Starred in your Ch 9 chapter file. His logic: In the intro he defines adaptation as adjusting by changing which genes are switched on, WITHOUT changing the genes themselves. Options A and B are both just gene-expression changes, so they count as adaptation (innate immunity does them too). Only C changes the genes themselves, and he says the adaptive system "deliberately mutates genes" (this is somatic hypermutation of B cells). That is what goes beyond adaptation. Search words: adjustments, hypermutation, somatic. Go to: PDF p1, the intro paragraph that defines "adaptation"; PDF p20 for the mechanism.
